subsections.name: Sri Vaishnava & South Indian Vaishnava Traditions

adjacencies.rationale: Sri Chand provides an historical connection; retain separate tradition identities.
Move from Punjab/Udasin context into Himalayan monastic settings. This is a layout choice, not one common lineage.
Follow the upper-Ganga to Kashi ascetic corridor; keep Kriya together where reviewed and cross-reference its eastern locations.
Tulsidas/Kashi and Rama/Avadh provide visitor-facing connections without redrawing family memberships.
Rama devotion leads into the existing Ramanandi subsection; sharing devotion does not establish a genealogical link.
Use already reviewed Ramanandi/Braj bridge displays, including the existing Mira/Ravidas/Kabir curatorial story where present and supported; do not create new relationships.
Goswami/Vrindavan anchors move naturally from Braj’s wider devotional landscape into Gaudiya history.
Priority boundary: Chaitanya and the Vrindavan Goswamis connect Braj, Bengal and Puri. Put the Gaudiya subsection at Braj’s exit and the Puri subsection at the East entrance.
A distinct eastern/Bihar contemplative interval; do not imply Buddhism descends from Jagannath devotion.
Broaden from Bihar/eastern sacred geography into Bengal’s varied traditions; keep identities explicit.

adjacencies.toSubsection: Sri Vaishnava & South Indian Vaishnava Traditions
adjacencies.rationale: Weakest boundary: use a concise East–South orientation panel. Puri–Srirangam/Gopala Bhatta and modern Bengal–Puducherry are cross-references to named displays, not a claimed Bengal-Shakta-to-Sri-Vaishnava lineage.

adjacencies.fromSubsection: Sri Vaishnava & South Indian Vaishnava Traditions
adjacencies.rationale: Introduce southern Vaishnava and Shaiva sacred landscapes side by side without collapsing their philosophies.
Arunachala provides a Tamil/Shaiva sacred-landscape connection; Ramana’s Advaita identity remains distinct.
Move from a named contemplative centre into neighbouring southern avadhuta/Advaita contexts. No universal guru chain is asserted.
Priority boundary: southern Datta/avadhuta contexts meet western Datta displays. Narasimha Saraswati’s Karnataka/Maharashtra landscape provides a named story. Keep independent families distinct.
Continue into Maharashtra’s connected guru settings; use only reviewed named relationships, not an all-saints Datta umbrella.
Move from guru-centred networks into Pandharpur/Vitthal devotional communities while retaining their separate groupings.
Dnyaneshwar/Nivrittinath’s Nath context offers a specific bridge toward Nath material; no claim that all Varkaris are Nath or directly connected to all Girnar saints.
Finish the western route in Gujarat’s institutional/devotional landscape. This is geography and visitor flow, not a single lineage.

conditionalContext.placement: Optional entrance orientation or exit reflection if confirmed holdings justify it; not a compulsory seventh numbered region.

tradeoffs: Physical visitor order differs from book chapter order: Sikh before Himalaya, South before West. Preserve book chapter reference separately; do not repurpose stable IDs or present visitor positions as book chapter numbers.
East-to-South is an editorial hinge, not a direct lineage chain; cross-reference named Puri/Srirangam and modern Puducherry stories.
Buddhist Saints is kept as a distinct subsection within the East; its neighbours are regional/comparative, not a genealogy.
Kriya’s Himalayan anchor cannot also place all its eastern contexts directly adjacent in a strict line; use one cross-reference panel without splitting the reviewed family.
A single line cannot keep Datta simultaneously adjacent to both southern Andhra and Girnar; place it at the South–West boundary and cross-reference Girnar internally.
If entry/exit location demands it, reverse the complete region and within-region sequence together to preserve every adjacency. No proposed cabinet moves are inferred.

If book chapter order must remain the physical order, retain it as an alternative but accept weaker East–West and West–South boundary links; the preferred order optimizes the stated Gaudiya and southern-Datta bridges.
